newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BUX a bit firmer in lowest turnover.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BUX a bit firmer in lowest turnover.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange closed the week with the lowest daily spot share turnover of this year while the BUX index rose a shade.
The BUX index finished at 5,315.46 points, up 14.31.
BUX futures gained ground for all maturities adding by between 20 and 42.50 points with the nearest June maturity closing firmer by the upper end of the range.
"Foreigners virtually showed no activity at all," said Tamas Revesz of Wintrust.
On Friday chemicals stocks posted relatively good gains with Borsodchem rising 90 forints to 6,200 and TVK advancing 30 forints to 2,300.
Plastics group Pannonplast, which announced this morning that it had boosted its stake and raised the capital in one of its subsidiaries, put on 100 forints to end at 7,900.
Traders said oil company MOL's market is ailing. "There's no speculation in MOL," Revesz said.
In slack volume of 34,493 shares MOL closed at 3,000 forints, up five. "Everybody is sitting on his or her MOL portfolio, they accepted this price level."
MOL's price is seen remaining rangebound until details of its planned new phase of privatisation go through the market.

On the negative side trading company Csopak plummeted more than six percent or 190 forints to close at 2,900 forints. The price fall stemmed from a sell order for 10,000 shares, one trader said, adding the deal was fulfilled.
R&D firm Horizon-Multiplan was suspended after one single deal due to too sharp an intraday fall, traders said. In that deal Horizon traded at 230 forints, down 60.
Analysts said a substantial recovery on the Hungarian market was unlikely for at least a month.

"There will not be significant movements until the first quarter corporate results are published," said Tommy Erdei, analyst at ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett in Budapest. "Funds, particulary the new ones, will only select shares for their portfolio after that."
Analysts said if the Dow continues to suffer heavy losses the Budapest bourse may detach itself and go its own way.
"If the Dow falls for a long time investors may look at this market because it still offers good opportunities," Erdei said.
